Being interested in me for who I am, not who I'm friends with, what I work as, how much money I have, what I look like... Everyone is pretty weird deep inside and real friends will try to understand you and see your darkest traits in a positive light. If you're only interested in the outer shell you have no value to me as a friend and is probably boring/shallow as fuck as a person. Unfortunately people nowadays seem so engrossed about themselves that they don't even consider the immense depth of other people.

Also I'm pretty introverted so unless someone is willing to take the initiative and ask me out to do stuff I'm probably not calling them either. This is a personal weakness and a flaw in me but it's who I am. I hope I can work on this later but right now if people don't want to call me to hang out or something there is little chance of maintaining a stable friendship.

One last thing, probably most important: good friends stab you in the front. People who see your flaws and won't talk to you about them or who get offended and keep it to themselves are not friends - they offer no opportunity for growth. Someone who is only there to agree with you and make you feel good even when you're being stupid is not a friend, but a follower, and most probably wants something from you. Other people exist (in a sense) to see the things about yourself that you just can't, because you are on the pilot seat and can't see the outside. Real friends must offer constructive criticism when it is warranted and validate you by supporting you, being there when you need it or just having fun together. Otherwise they are mere acquaintances - even if you are together all the time - or Facebook friends (more like contacts, really) and many people can't tell the difference between these and true friendship.

"Politically correct games? Really?" -- Editorial on Germany's most respected computer news site. [translation within]

Editorial: Politically correct games? For real??

The sexism in video games debate is over the top. Gaming means letting off steam and having fun. Nobody needs politically correct games.

Since my childhood I was roaming digital worlds, first on Sega consoles, later on the PC. I crawled through dark catacombs, I made it rain in Duke Nukem 3D, and enjoyed blowing up skyscraper-tall bosses with BFGs. Over the years I observed how gaming went from one dimensional simplicity to interesting, multi-layered stories.

Gothic 2 was one of the mile stones and opened a world to gamers in which they could self-actualize. Some of the current games tell complex interwoven stories that gamers from 15 years ago could only dream about. The Last of Us and GTA V are very good, if very different examples to describe this new generation of games. Escapism through immersion on the highest level.

Without a question, sexism is a problem in our Western world, too. But when it comes to the subject of Anita Sarkeesian, well that was irritating. Although I'm not sure if I was irritated because she stupidly focused on games like GTA, i.e. games that use social satire and exaggeration. Or because she calculatingly and manipulatively focused on games like it. Either way it didn't make the debate any more objective and the waves she made only popularized her, but less so her goal.

Her cherry-picking of sexist scenes and taking them out of sometimes complex contexts led to -once again- to a revolt amongst many gamers who fear for their digital worlds. It's a terrible thing that a few fanatics intimidated Mrs. Sarkeesian so much she had to fled her home. But should this set the tone for the debate on sexism in games? No!

It's not like the image of women in video games is actually limited to damsels in distress or willing prostitutes. There has been lots of positive change in games over the years. For instance most role playing games are created for both female and male gamers. Yes, there are still stereotypes -- but there are both female and male stereotypes. Thus I don't believe that the sexism critics are doing themselves any favors with the way they're conducting this -actually important- debate.

Also... why just a debate about sexism in games? How about violence? Racism? Speeding? We're talking about GAMES in which you can let off steam because nobody actually gets hurts if you kill somebody. Politically correct games? For real??

Haha, he rambled and repeated a bit but it's pretty good. Although one of the big things they like to claim they're "necessary" for is 'politics' in gaming.

I would have personally backed up with examples that we already have politics in gaming, the good kind of politics. 4x games are all about managing an unruly population of course, but then there's the cyberpunk genre like Net Gain, Shadowrun, and Syndicate, there's a plethora of environmentalist-themed games, there's economy games with trading like MULE and Taipan and their successors, a plethora of games with coloured or other minority leads (Urban Chaos being one of the best box-tickers, which hasn't made the jump to next-gen unfortunately for some reason.), and there's been female-led AND programmed AND written games going all the way back to 1984.

Practically the only actual thing they can hit on is there's no "trans" leads, but come on, do you really think someone trying to make a living is gonna risk it on something guaranteed to have no reach and receive no money? If they actually cared about activism they'd realise how much more expensive/time-consuming making games were, and go out and change society first before coming back to bitch about that. In order for a trans-led game to be profitable, every single one of them would need to buy it, no matter whether they liked the genre or intended to play it or not. So far the closest we've gotten is Mr/Ms herm fanservice from Nier, they'd never have gotten away with if they made it look 'realistic' like how they want, which seems to be basing a transgender person on either Wu or Brice.

IMO since bulky action heroes are the most common thing out there ever since CoD got popular, you will most likely see a Trans MAN first, as they could get away with barely modifying a pre-existing model.

They apparently do not feel a transwoman should ever try to 'pass' and 'act sane' so they would never accept anyone's interpretation of a transwoman other than their own.

If they really want to blame anyone for the lack of representation lately, they should have joined GG in helping them unearth shady Big Corp practices, rather than being dumbasses and shielding them, as it seems there was a very coerced shift back in 2005 when G4 forced gaming mainstream to hit a bigger audience. The biggest studios stopped taking chances afterwards, and those that banked on chancey game mechanics/storylines like Psygnosis couldn't adapt to the new (and somewhat oversaturated now) market.
